title: The Torah and the Tanakh
examples: How is a Torah scroll made?

explain.say: The Torah is the most sacred text of Judaism. Torah means teaching or instruction, and it is made of five books, which Jewish tradition says were given by God to Moses at Mount Sinai.

draw.text: Also called the Five Books of Moses, or the Pentateuch

explain.say: The five books are Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. In Hebrew each is named after an early word in it, like Bereshit, in the beginning, for Genesis.

items: English | Hebrew name | What it tells
Genesis | Bereshit | Creation, Abraham to Joseph
Exodus | Shemot | Slavery in Egypt, freedom, Sinai
Numbers | Bamidbar | Forty years in the wilderness

explain.say: At the heart of the Torah is the story of the Exodus: the Israelites leave slavery in Egypt, receive the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai, and travel through the wilderness to the edge of the promised land.

draw.label: The Exodus story: from Egypt to Sinai to the Jordan (traditional route, simplified)

draw.text: Passover remembers the Exodus each spring

explain.say: The Torah is the first part of the Tanakh, the Hebrew Bible. Tanakh is made from the first letters of its three parts: Torah, the teaching; Nevi'im, the prophets; and Ketuvim, the writings, 24 books in all.

In a synagogue the Torah is read from a handwritten scroll, the Sefer Torah, copied by a trained scribe on parchment. A portion is read each week, so the whole Torah is completed every year, and the reader follows the words with a pointer called a yad.

draw.text: About 304,805 letters, each written by hand

explain.say: Jewish tradition sees the Torah as given at Sinai, while many scholars think it was gathered from older sources and reached its final form around the 5th century BCE. Alongside it, the oral Torah was later written down in the Mishnah and the Talmud.

items: Tradition: the Torah given to Moses at Sinai
Many scholars: final form about 5th century BCE
About 200 CE: the Mishnah written down
About 500 CE: the Babylonian Talmud completed
Today: read in synagogues every week

draw.text: 613 commandments, the mitzvot, in rabbinic counting

faq.a: The Torah is the most sacred text of Judaism: the five books of Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. The word means teaching or instruction, and in a wider sense Torah can mean all Jewish teaching.
asks: What does Torah mean?
What is in the Torah?
Why is the Torah important?

faq.q: What are the five books of the Torah?
faq.a: They are Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. In Hebrew they are Bereshit, Shemot, Vayikra, Bamidbar and Devarim.
asks: Name the five books of Moses
What is the Pentateuch?
How many books are in the Torah?

faq.a: The Tanakh is the Hebrew Bible. Its name comes from the first letters of its three parts: Torah, the teaching; Nevi'im, the prophets; and Ketuvim, the writings.
asks: What does Tanakh stand for?
What is the Hebrew Bible?
What are Nevi'im and Ketuvim?

faq.q: How many books are in the Tanakh?
faq.a: Jewish tradition counts 24 books. They contain the same writings as the 39 books of the Protestant Old Testament, but some are counted together, such as the twelve shorter prophets as one book.
asks: Why does the Tanakh have 24 books?
Is the Tanakh the same as the Old Testament?
How many books does the Hebrew Bible have?

faq.a: Jewish tradition holds that God gave the Torah to Moses, which is why it is called the Five Books of Moses. Many modern scholars think it was woven together from several older sources and reached its final form around the 5th century BCE.
asks: Did Moses write the Torah?
Who is the author of the Torah?
Where did the Torah come from?

faq.a: A Torah scroll, or Sefer Torah, is a handwritten copy of the five books on parchment, rolled on two wooden poles. It is kept in the ark of a synagogue and treated with great respect.
asks: What is a Sefer Torah?
Why is the Torah a scroll?
Where is the Torah kept?

faq.q: How is a Torah scroll made?
faq.a: A trained scribe, called a sofer, writes every letter by hand with a quill and special ink on parchment, about 304,805 letters in all. It can take around a year, and a single mistake must be carefully corrected.
asks: Who writes a Torah scroll?
How long does it take to write a Torah?
How many letters are in the Torah?

faq.q: Why do people use a pointer to read the Torah?
faq.a: The pointer, called a yad, which means hand, lets the reader follow the words without touching the parchment. This protects the scroll and shows respect for the sacred text.
asks: What is a yad?
Why don't they touch the Torah?
What is the Torah pointer for?

faq.q: How often is the Torah read?
faq.a: A portion, called a parashah, is read in the synagogue every Sabbath, with shorter readings on Mondays and Thursdays. The whole Torah is read through in a year, and the festival of Simchat Torah celebrates finishing and starting again.
asks: What is a parashah?
What is Simchat Torah?
Is the Torah read every week?

faq.a: The Ten Commandments are laws that the Torah says God gave at Mount Sinai, found in Exodus chapter 20 and Deuteronomy chapter 5. They include worshipping one God, keeping the Sabbath, honouring parents, and not killing, stealing or lying.
asks: Where are the Ten Commandments in the Torah?
What happened at Mount Sinai?
Are the Ten Commandments in the Torah?

faq.a: Rabbinic tradition counts 613 commandments, or mitzvot, in the Torah: 248 positive ones, things to do, and 365 negative ones, things not to do. They cover prayer, festivals, food, justice and kindness.
asks: What are mitzvot?
How many laws are in the Torah?
What is a mitzvah?

faq.a: Jewish tradition holds that alongside the written Torah, Moses received explanations passed down by word of mouth. These were later written down in the Mishnah, around 200 CE, and discussed in the Talmud.
asks: What is the Talmud?
What is the Mishnah?
Is there more to the Torah than the five books?

faq.a: The Shema is a central Jewish prayer from Deuteronomy chapter 6: Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One. Many Jews say it every morning and evening.
asks: What is the most important Jewish prayer?
Where does the Shema come from?
What does Hear O Israel mean?

faq.q: What is a bar or bat mitzvah?
faq.a: A bar mitzvah, for boys at 13, or bat mitzvah, for girls at 12 or 13, marks becoming responsible for keeping the commandments. Often the young person reads from the Torah scroll in the synagogue for the first time.
asks: Why do Jewish children read the Torah at 13?
What happens at a bar mitzvah?
What is a bat mitzvah?

facts: The Torah has five books: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.
Tanakh stands for Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim, and Jewish tradition counts 24 books in it.
A Torah scroll is handwritten by a trained scribe, a sofer, and has about 304,805 letters.
Rabbinic tradition counts 613 commandments, or mitzvot, in the Torah.
The whole Torah is read in synagogue over a year, and Simchat Torah celebrates finishing and beginning again.
